narrative.northStar: The Reading Lamp, opened into a personal reading room
narrative.overview:
Creative north star: The Reading Lamp, opened into a personal reading room.
Librarium should feel like the maintainer's sophisticated Warhammer and Black Library
home. Literata titles, generous composition, the supplied archivist artwork and
coherent themes invite browsing. Engineering remains powerful and discoverable
from the book, series or active task.

The [UX standards](docs/ux-standards.md) own hierarchy, truth, disclosure,
composition, artwork admission, accessibility and acceptance. This file translates
that direction into visual treatments. The final L024 direction replaces the
compact-row mandate; it preserves Reading Lamp's identity and interaction quality.

The [Reading Room concept](images/inspiration/librarium-03-reading-room.png)
supplies literary atmosphere, reading comfort and a confident relationship between
book and artwork. Its reader layout, chapters, cover and claims are illustrative.
The target opens in Shelves: responsive book entries with admitted real art and
title-led folios where art is unavailable. A remembered List option supports
focused scanning. Both preserve the source series order. No cover availability
or reader feature is claimed by this design record.

The frontmatter and sidecar are the current **design target**, not a generated
inventory of shipping CSS or rendered acceptance. Their readable scale replaces
the earlier 15px/58px prescription. Frontend alignment and runtime verification
belong to the implementing task and [status](docs/status.md). Control height
values are minimums; text and wrapping may always increase them. The legacy
`work-row` token key now describes the folio treatment for existing consumers.
keyCharacteristics: Books, titles, authors and series carry the visual interest; ink surfaces, artwork and thematic color support them.
Literata gives book and page titles a reading voice; system sans keeps controls and evidence precise.
A 16px body target, larger book titles and generous folio padding support reading. Authors and series have their own readable space.
Bounded reading measures, quiet navigation and useful grouping create rhythm.
Selected-work detail preserves the route back to the same browsing position.
Genuine supplied artwork and bounded folio motion keep the identity distinctive.

rules.name: The Teal Means Here Rule
rules.body: Teal identifies action, focus, selection and live state. Its meaning stays consistent through every theme.

rules.name: The One Fill Rule
rules.body: Selected Ink marks a selected work or browsing choice; the current navigation destination uses an accent underline. Pressed Ink marks hover/active interaction. Hover is gated by `(hover: hover)`.

rules.name: The Color Has a Job Rule
rules.body: Copper supports identity and headings, teal supports interaction, and rose accompanies failure wording and recovery. Color alone carries no status claim.

rules.name: The Reading Voice Rule
rules.body: Literata sets book and page titles; the supplied SVG sets the wordmark. Controls, labels and figures use system sans.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Counts, recorded positions, pages and progress use tabular numerals where stable alignment aids comparison.

rules.name: The Readable Core Rule
rules.body: Authors, series and meaningful status remain reading content. Their legibility is not traded for more records in the viewport.

rules.name: The Keep Your Place Rule
rules.body: Selecting a work preserves the browsing context; Back restores its query, page, scroll and focus. Polling does not reset the view.

rules.name: The Readable Folio Rule
rules.body: A work gets a prominent title and separate readable author/series context. Shelves uses 1.15rem padding and a 10rem minimum; List uses 0.85rem by 0.75rem padding and an 82px minimum, growing freely for content. Fixed two-line records and a single metadata line are not requirements.

rules.name: The Recorded Order Rule
rules.body: Display recorded positions literally. Numbered nonzero positions come first in ascending order, then records at 0, then records without a position. Label the later groups with their real counts. An unknown position is announced as No position. Never invent sequence or omit a work.

dos: Follow docs/ux-standards.md for hierarchy, status, disclosure, composition, cover admission and acceptance.
Treat concrete tokens and specimens as the current target; verify actual frontend/rendered alignment.
Default Shelves and remembered List preserve source series order; admitted art enriches entries and absent art keeps title-led folios.
Keep available synopsis visible above quieter engineering controls.
Preserve supplied identity, themes, advanced capabilities and the return path.
donts: Do not optimize the home for maximum database-row density.
Do not fabricate shipping covers, ownership claims or source evidence.
Do not hide actionable warnings or technical facts needed to interpret or recover from a result.
